description.en: Memory plugins for DeepSeek Harness: one unified surface, eight tools, one short standing injection.
description.zh: DeepSeek Harness 的记忆插件索引：一套统一工具面、一段最短常驻注入。

description.en: One memory plugin instead of three: 8 unified memory_* tools and a single 1,235-character injection, with meow-memory's seven-layer SQLite as the main store and a rebuildable graph index. Tool schemas 56,759 B → 13,567 B (−76.1%), standing prompt 4,085 → 1,235 chars (−69.8%). Nothing was dropped: writes land in the main store first, graph links that cannot be written are queued instead of lost, and the setting page takes effect without a restart. 0.4.0 adds query decomposition, write-time consolidation, supersede + inflation checks, an entity layer on the graph, and co-occurrence query expansion learned from your own keywords — every one of them has an off switch and an on/off reading. 0.5.0 bridges CJK word forms so a paraphrase still lands. 0.6.0 makes scoring scale-adaptive: on a 660-entry snapshot, verbatim hit@1 0.895 → 0.921 and paraphrased 0.333 → 0.417 with zero wrong flips, and every hit now carries its `status`. 0.6.1 turns the three-trees-out-of-sync problem into one command (`tools/sync-trees.mjs`, dry-run by default, never deletes), pins the adaptive-idf wiring with two static regexes so a silent behaviour regression cannot pass green, and fixes a `%20` path bug in a maintenance script — engine bytes unchanged. 0.6.2 fixes a recall bug where the store said nothing when something was there: the noise floor dropped the only matchable word and left a word that does not exist in the store in its place (8 of 1,531 English questions came back empty). It now rescues only the words the noise floor dropped and never function words, so empty replies went 0.52% → 0 while hit@1/5/10/20, MRR and the 660-entry snapshot readings stayed bit-identical. 0.6.3 makes answers reproducible: a tie on score used to fall back to corpus order (V8's stable sort), so the same question could give two different top-tens depending on how the store happened to lay the rows out. The ladder now ends with updated-later-first and a natural id order, the adaptive-idf cluster pick no longer breaks ties by array index, and no ordering step uses localeCompare — and every reading stayed bit-identical. 0.6.4 fixes single-character queries: the tokenizer only emits CJK bigrams, so a one-hanzi question yields no tokens and the retrieval gate treated “cannot tokenize” as “not in memory” — the most direct questions (`读`, `钱`, `花`) always came back empty. It now falls back to a literal substring pass over title/content/keywords only when the query is a single CJK code point and tokenization produced nothing, still going through the same ordering ladder; English stopwords and punctuation stay closed. Every reading is bit-identical — this restores reachability, not ranking. 0.6.5 fixes punctuated single-character queries: the 0.6.4 gate demanded exactly one code point, yet a one-hanzi question almost always carries punctuation — `读？`, `钱。`, `花！`, `「读」` all came back empty. The gate now strips punctuation and whitespace first and requires exactly one remaining hanzi, allowing only punctuation/whitespace beside it; letters, digits and symbols stay closed, and a repeated character counts once. Every reading is bit-identical again — reachability, not ranking. 0.6.6 fixes dirty memories: `...d.keywords` in `docText` threw `TypeError: d.keywords is not iterable` for entries whose keywords were missing, null, or a comma-joined string (imported rows, rows written by other plugins, caller-built docs) — not one missing hit, but a whole failed search. Keywords now go through `kwList`: arrays, comma/ideographic-comma strings and JSON strings all count, and `docText`, the scoring fields `kwToks`/`kwSets`, `keywordHitScore` and the index signature all use it (comma-joined keywords finally reach tf-idf). Every reading is bit-identical — reachability again, not ranking. 0.6.7 fixes broken rows: a single null / undefined / scalar entry in `docs` (half-written rows, truncated imports, a caller passing ids instead of objects) made `docText` throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'title')`, and a non-array `docs` died on `docs.length`. Both entry points now pass a gate `liveDocs(docs)`: non-arrays return empty, entries are checked for object-ness, filtering happens only when something is broken, and a clean array is returned as the same reference (the index cache is keyed by a content signature, not identity, so nothing is invalidated); an all-broken array returns empty rather than scoring null as a memory. Every reading is bit-identical. 0.6.8 is about the lifetime of the checks themselves: versions, suite counts, assertion totals and time budgets all advance every release, so writing them as equality turns every bump into a false failure (`0.2.31→35` hit it four times; `0.6.2→0.6.7` hand-bumped `steps.length === 35 → 36` each time and edited two hand-copied doc numbers). Suite count is now a floor (`SUITE_FLOOR`: adding a suite needs no edit, losing one fails immediately), the current numbers in the docs are reconciled automatically against the baseline totals, historical milestones keep their own numbers, and the version ladder is compared by version, not layout. The engine is byte-identical; every reading is the same. 0.6.9 measures the ruler first: since 0.3.0 every published reading came from a single pass in a single order (corpus in storage order, questions in fixture order), and those single-pass numbers are exactly what rejected three candidates (English stemming, MMR, coverage re-rank). If the ruler is order-sensitive, those negatives carry the ruler own noise. `tools/probe-rigor.mjs` now pins seven properties: three consecutive passes give bit-identical readings (std = 0), reversed corpus order, three shuffles (seed 3/11/42), reversed question order, a second independent scorer, an injected same-score-corpus-order bias that must go red (A/B top-1 hits 23 to 15), and fixed tier sizes 45/14/10. On 69 real-corpus questions: hit@1 0.9565 / hit@3 0.9855 / MRR 0.9686, unchanged across passes and orders. The engine is byte-identical; LoCoMo and real-corpus readings are unchanged. 0.6.10 removes a fixed per-query cost: the search-index cache key is a content signature, and while the usual answer is that the store did not change, the price was paid in full every time. On four isomorphic corpora (660 / 2,000 / 5,000 / 10,000) the signature consumed 28.8%-30.6% of a warm search (0.96 / 2.84 / 7.04 / 14.16 ms). It is now accounted per document: a WeakMap keyed by the doc holds a 32-bit per-doc hash plus a snapshot of the fields that feed it, compared by value (not object identity) before reuse; the per-doc hash had to be lifted out of the rolling value to be cacheable at all; shapes whose values cannot be compared fall back to direct computation. Signatures now cost 0.062 / 0.189 / 0.528 / 1.198 ms (15x, share down to 2.8%-3.5%) and a warm search 3.24 to 2.18, 9.67 to 6.80, 23.0 to 15.3, 49.2 to 37.6 ms. Ranking is byte-identical; LoCoMo and real-corpus readings are unchanged. 0.6.11 keeps paying down fixed cost: the remaining warm-search time is now accounted per channel, and the most expensive one is verbatim matching, which used to rebuild one lowercased string of the whole store on every query (id + project + title + content + keywords) just to answer whether an identifier appears verbatim, 2.03 MB at 10,000 docs and 35.7%-50.6% of a warm search; splitting that further showed 5.78 ms spent building strings against 0.51 ms of actual scanning. The haystack now lives in the index next to the token table, is built per document on demand and accounted (built / reused), and nothing is built when the query carries no identifier. The same change closed a 0.6.10 hole: the haystack contains project, project was never part of the signature, and once the string is cached a changed project would have been served from a stale index. Warm search: 2.04 to 1.62, 5.04 to 4.20, 11.88 to 9.12, 24.45 to 18.82 ms (-20.6% / -16.7% / -23.2% / -23.0%), verbatim share down to 18.6%-34.9%. Ranking is byte-identical; LoCoMo and real-corpus readings are unchanged. Self-checked by 40 suites / 3,683 executable assertions in about 220 seconds.
description.zh: 一个记忆插件顶三个：8 个统一 memory_* 工具 + 一段 1,235 字符常驻注入，主库仍是 meow-memory 的七层 SQLite，星图退成可重建的索引。工具 schema 56,759 B → 13,567 B（−76.1%），常驻注入 4,085 → 1,235 字符（−69.8%）。能力一条没砍：写入先落主库，连不上星图的连线排队不丢，设置页改完即刻生效、不用重启。0.4.0 又加了查询分解、写入巩固、自动取代与通胀体检、实体层、以及从你自己的 keywords 学出来的共现扩词——每一件都有开关，也都有开/关对照读数；0.5.0 用 CJK 词形桥让换说法也能落地。0.6.0 让打分随库规模自适应：660 条快照上照抄 hit@1 0.895 → 0.921、换说法 0.333 → 0.417、误伤 0，每条命中顺带带 `status`。0.6.1 把「三棵树没同步」做成一条命令（`tools/sync-trees.mjs`，默认只体检、从不删除），用两条静态正则钉住自适应 idf 的接线点（判据全绿但行为回退这种沉默故障过不去），并修掉一个维护脚本的 `%20` 路径 bug——引擎字节未变。0.6.2 修的是一个把「有」说成「没有」的缺陷：噪声地板剔掉了唯一能命中的词、留下库里根本不存在（df=0）的词顶位，1,531 条英文问句里 8 条回执为空；处方只救被噪声地板剔掉的词（虚词一个都不救），空回 0.52% → 0，hit@1/5/10/20、MRR 与 660 条快照三档读数逐位不变。0.6.3 让答案是可复现的：分数并列时以前会退回语料顺序（V8 稳定排序），同一个问句能因为存储布局不同给出两套前十；定序梯子现在末尾是「更新得更晚的在前」+ id 自然序，自适应 idf 挑簇不再按数组下标破平，整条链上也没有 localeCompare——所有读数逐位不变。0.6.4 修的是「一个汉字也是问题」：分词只产二元组，一个汉字的问句切出来是空数组，检索的第一道门就把「切不出词」当成「没有」，于是 `读`/`钱`/`花` 这类最直白的问法永远空手。现在只在「切不出词 + 单个汉字」时按原文子串在标题、正文与关键词里找一次，仍走同一套定序；英文停用词与标点一个都不放行。所有读数逐位不变——修的是可达性，不是排序。0.6.5 修的是「标点也是人打的」：0.6.4 的单字兜底只认「正好一个码点」，可人问一个字的时候问号几乎从不缺席——`读？`、`钱。`、`花！`、`「读」` 一个都回不来。现在把标点与空白剥掉再数，剥完正好剩一个汉字才走兜底，汉字之外只许标点或空白；字母、数字、符号一律不放行，同一个字重复按一个算。所有读数又是一位没动——修的仍是可达性，不是排序。0.6.6 修的是「脏记忆不许把整次检索打成异常」：`docText` 里的 `...d.keywords` 遇上缺字段 / `null` / 逗号串（导入行、别的插件写的行、调用方自拼的 docs）会抛 `TypeError: d.keywords is not iterable`——不是少一条命中，是整次检索一个回执都拿不回来。现在 keywords 统一走 `kwList`：数组、逗号顿号串、JSON 串都认，`docText`、打分面的 `kwToks`/`kwSets`、`keywordHitScore` 与索引签名全走它（逗号串的关键词从此真进 tf-idf）。读数一位没动，修的是可达性。0.6.7 修的是「一条坏行不许把整次检索打成异常」：`docs` 里混进一条 `null` / `undefined` / 标量（半写的行、导入截断、调用方把 id 列表当 docs），`docText` 的 `d.title` 会抛 `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'title')`；`docs` 整个不是数组时死在 `docs.length`。现在两个入口都过闸 `liveDocs(docs)`：非数组回空、逐条问「是不是对象」、脏了才过滤，干净数组原样返回同一引用（索引缓存的键是内容签名，不靠身份，缓存不会被打掉）；全是坏行时回空，不把 `null` 当一条记忆打分。读数一位没动。0.6.8 治的是判据自己的寿命：版本号、支数、断言总数、耗时预算每版都在动，写成等值就每升一版必红一次（`0.2.31→35` 四遍版本等值、`0.6.2→0.6.7` 每版手工抬 `steps.length === 35 → 36` 并连带改两处手抄的「N 支 / M 条」）。现在支数是地板 `SUITE_FLOOR`（只许加不许减，减一支立刻红、加一支不必动判据），文档里「现在」的数由探针读基线合计自动对账，历史里程碑冻结自己那版的数字，版本阶梯按版本号比。引擎一个字节没动，读数逐位相同。0.6.9 先量了尺子：0.3.0 起所有对外读数都是单次、单序量出来的（语料按库里顺序、问句按夹具顺序、跑一遍取一个数），而这一路正是拿这些单次数否决过三个候选（英文词形归一、MMR、覆盖率重排）——量尺若对顺序敏感，那些「负数」里就掺着量尺自己的噪声。现在 `tools/probe-rigor.mjs` 钉住七条：连跑 3 次三档读数逐位相同（std = 0）、语料倒序、三种打乱（seed 3/11/42）、问句倒序、独立 scorer 交叉验、进程内注入「同分按语料序」的偏置必红（A/B 互换第一名命中 23→15）、分档口径 45/14/10。真库样张 69 问 hit@1 0.9565 / hit@3 0.9855 / MRR 0.9686，三次与换序后一个字都不差。引擎一个字节没动，LoCoMo 与真库读数逐位不变。0.6.10 治的是每问一次的固定开销：索引缓存的键是内容签名，而「库没变」这个答案几乎每回都成立，代价却每次全额付。四条同构语料（660 / 2,000 / 5,000 / 10,000）上签名占一次热检索 28.8%–30.6%（0.96 / 2.84 / 7.04 / 14.16 ms）。改后按条记账：WeakMap 以 doc 为键存条级 32 位哈希与字段值快照，逐字段比较值（不是对象身份），全等才复用；条级哈希从滚动值里拆出来才能缓存；判不出有没有变的形状走直算。读数：签名 0.062 / 0.189 / 0.528 / 1.198 ms（15×）、占比降到 2.8%–3.5%，一次热检索 3.24→2.18、9.67→6.80、23.0→15.3、49.2→37.6 ms。排序一个字节没动，LoCoMo 与真库读数逐位不变。0.6.11 接着算固定开销：把热检索剩下的钱按通道拆开点名，最贵的一块是原样匹配——为了回答「这条里有没有原样出现这个标识符」，它每问一次都把整库拼成一份小写大字符串（id + project + title + content + keywords），10,000 条就是 2.03 MB，占一次热检索 35.7%–50.6%（660/2,000/5,000/10,000 条实测）；再拆一层，造串 5.78 ms 而真正的扫描只要 0.51 ms。改后 haystack 跟切词表一样搬进索引、按条懒建并记账（built / reused），问句里没有标识符时一条都不建；顺手补掉 0.6.10 的洞：haystack 含 project 而 project 从不进签名，搬进索引后就会「改 project 拿旧串答新库」，故 project 补进签名与值比较。读数：全量检索 2.04→1.62、5.04→4.20、11.88→9.12、24.45→18.82 ms（−20.6% / −16.7% / −23.2% / −23.0%），原样匹配份额降到 18.6%–34.9%。排序一个字节没动：LoCoMo 与真库读数逐位不变。自检 40 支、3,683 条可执行断言、约 220 秒跑完。
